title: Láttam, láttad, látta...: The Full Past of lát

sections.title: A fully regular transitive verb
sections.content: lát ("to see") is regular — no stem change at all — so it's the clearest place to watch the indefinite/definite split work exactly the way you'd predict. Unlike találkozik, lát does take a direct object, so both rows genuinely differ: láttam is "I saw (something/someone)", láttam a barátomat is "I saw my friend" and still uses láttam (1sg is always identical), but from (te) on the two rows split apart: láttad, látta, láttuk...

items.spanish: Láttam egy szép kabátot a kirakatban.
items.english: I saw a nice coat in the shop window.
I haven't seen Tamás in a long time.

sections.content: The rule from present tense carries over unchanged: egy kabátot or no article at all → indefinite (láttam); a/az + noun, a possessive, or a name → definite (láttam a kabátot, láttam Tamást — a name still counts as definite, even with no article).
